title: JSON with Yojson: parsing, validating and printing
body: JSON is the common format for configuration and web APIs, and Yojson is the usual OCaml library for it. `Yojson.Safe.from_string` parses text into a variant tree: `` `Assoc `` for objects, `` `List `` for arrays, `` `String ``, `` `Int ``, `` `Float ``, `` `Bool `` and `` `Null ``. Malformed text raises `Yojson.Json_error`, so a parser for untrusted input must catch it.

The `Yojson.Safe.Util` module reads values out of the tree: `member "port" json` returns the field, or `` `Null `` when it is missing, and `to_int`, `to_string` and `to_list` convert a value or raise `Type_error` when it has the wrong shape. Wrapping the whole conversion in one `try` turns every kind of bad input into a single `Error` message, which is the right boundary between untrusted text and your own typed record.

Printing goes the other way: build the variant tree from your record and call `Yojson.Safe.to_string`. Keep the conversion in both directions next to the type and test the round trip. For large schemas, `ppx_deriving_yojson` generates both functions from the type, in the same way `ppx_jane` derives s-expressions.
challenge: Implement `Appconfig.parse` so it turns a JSON object with `name` (string), `port` (int) and `tags` (list of strings) into the record, and returns `Error` with a message for invalid JSON or a missing or wrongly typed field. `to_json` is already written.
projectInstructions: Run `dune test --root .`. Edit only src/appconfig.ml. Remember that a missing field reads as `Null`, and that both `Yojson.Json_error` and `Yojson.Safe.Util.Type_error` can be raised.
question: What does `Yojson.Safe.Util.member "port" json` return when the field is missing?
correct: `Null, which a later to_int then rejects with a Type_error
reasoning: member is total, so absence shows up as Null, and the failure appears when the conversion function cannot accept it.
